BiblicalUsage: Hammath is a name that points two ways at once. Joshua lists it among the fenced cities of Naphtali, a place with walls and a territory. Chronicles names Hemath as the father of the house of Rechab, so the same spelling also belongs to a man.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the double use is worth stating plainly rather than smoothing over: one Hammath is a walled town, the other is a father, and the text does not confuse them even if the spelling is the same.
